transcribed: read from the Cadetprep Excel sheet by extract-cadetprep.ts (sheet row = n); key and solution are the source's, kept as evidence

questions.stem: Two people \(A\) and \(B\) start from points \(P\) and \(Q\) respectively, \(120\) km apart, and move towards each other with speeds \(30\) km/h and \(40\) km/h respectively. After how many hours will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
When two people move towards each other, relative speed = \(30 + 40 = 70\) km/h
Distance = \(120\) km
Time to meet = \(\frac{120}{70} = \frac{12}{7}\) hours

questions.stem: Two trains start from stations \(X\) and \(Y\), \(300\) km apart, and move towards each other at \(80\) km/h and \(70\) km/h respectively. They start at \(10:00\) AM. At what time will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(80 + 70 = 150\) km/h
Time to meet = \(\frac{300}{150} = 2\) hours
Meeting time = \(10:00\) AM + \(2\) hours = \(12:00\) PM

questions.stem: A person \(A\) starts from point \(P\) towards \(Q\) at \(40\) km/h. After \(2\) hours, person \(B\) starts from \(Q\) towards \(P\) at \(60\) km/h. If distance \(PQ = 480\) km, when will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
When \(B\) starts, \(A\) has covered \(40 \times 2 = 80\) km
Remaining distance = \(480 - 80 = 400\) km
Relative speed = \(40 + 60 = 100\) km/h
Time to meet from when \(B\) starts = \(\frac{400}{100} = 4\) hours
Total time from when \(A\) started = \(2 + 4 = 6\) hours

questions.stem: Two cyclists start from opposite ends of a \(150\) km track and cycle towards each other at \(25\) km/h and \(35\) km/h. How far from the starting point of the first cyclist will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Time to meet = \(\frac{150}{25 + 35} = \frac{150}{60} = 2.5\) hours
Distance covered by first cyclist = \(25 \times 2.5 = 62.5\) km
They meet \(62.5\) km from the first cyclist's starting point

questions.stem: Two persons \(A\) and \(B\) are \(200\) km apart. They start moving towards each other simultaneously at speeds \(50\) km/h and \(30\) km/h respectively. After meeting, they continue to their destinations. How much more time will \(B\) take to reach \(A's\) starting point than \(A\) takes to reach \(B's\) starting point?
questions.keySolution:
Time to meet = \(\frac{200}{50 + 30} = 2.5\) hours
Distance covered by \(A\) = \(50 \times 2.5 = 125\) km
Distance covered by \(B\) = \(30 \times 2.5 = 75\) km
After meeting, \(A\) needs to cover \(75\) km at \(50\) km/h = \(1.5\) hours
\(B\) needs to cover \(125\) km at \(30\) km/h = \(4.17\) hours
Difference = \(4.17 - 1.5 = 2.67\) hours ≈ \(2.5\) hours

questions.stem: A car and a bus start from points \(A\) and \(B\) towards each other at \(60\) km/h and \(40\) km/h respectively. They meet after \(3\) hours. What is the distance between \(A\) and \(B\)?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(60 + 40 = 100\) km/h
They meet after \(3\) hours
Distance = Speed × Time = \(100 \times 3 = 300\) km

questions.stem: Two trains running in opposite directions cross a man standing on the platform in \(15\) seconds and \(20\) seconds respectively. If their speeds are \(54\) km/h and \(36\) km/h, what is the sum of their lengths?
questions.keySolution:
Speed of first train = \(54\) km/h = \(54 \times \frac{5}{18} = 15\) m/s
Length of first train = \(15 \times 15 = 225\) m
Speed of second train = \(36\) km/h = \(36 \times \frac{5}{18} = 10\) m/s
Length of second train = \(10 \times 20 = 200\) m
Sum of lengths = \(225 + 200 = 425\) m

questions.stem: Two persons walking towards each other at \(4\) km/h and \(6\) km/h respectively, meet after \(2\) hours. If they were walking in the same direction, how long would it take for the faster person to overtake the slower one?
questions.keySolution:
When walking towards each other: Relative speed = \(4 + 6 = 10\) km/h
Distance between them initially = \(10 \times 2 = 20\) km
When walking in same direction: Relative speed = \(6 - 4 = 2\) km/h
Time to overtake = \(\frac{20}{2} = 10\) hours

questions.stem: A man walking at \(5\) km/h crosses a bridge in \(15\) minutes. A train \(150\) m long, travelling at \(45\) km/h, crosses the same bridge. How long does the train take?
questions.keySolution:
Length of bridge = \(5 \times \frac{15}{60} = 1.25\) km = \(1250\) m
Train speed = \(45\) km/h = \(45 \times \frac{5}{18} = 12.5\) m/s
Train has to cover bridge length + train length = \(1250 + 150 = 1400\) m
Time = \(\frac{1400}{12.5} = 112\) seconds

questions.stem: Two buses start from terminals \(200\) km apart and travel towards each other. The first bus travels \(20\) km in the first hour, \(25\) km in the second hour, \(30\) km in the third hour and so on. The second bus travels at a constant speed of \(40\) km/h. When will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Let them meet after \(t\) hours. First bus follows AP: \(a = 20\), \(d = 5\)
Distance by first bus in \(t\) hours = \(\frac{t}{2}[40 + 5(t-1)] = \frac{t(35 + 5t)}{2}\)
Distance by second bus = \(40t\)
Total = \(200\): \(\frac{t(35 + 5t)}{2} + 40t = 200\)
Solving: \(5t^2 + 115t - 400 = 0\) gives \(t = 2.5\) hours = \(2\) hours \(30\) minutes

questions.stem: Two friends start from their homes \(15\) km apart and walk towards each other at \(3\) km/h and \(2\) km/h respectively. A dog starts with the first friend, runs to the second friend, then back to the first, and so on until they meet. If the dog's speed is \(10\) km/h, what distance does the dog cover?
questions.keySolution:
Time for friends to meet = \(\frac{15}{3 + 2} = 3\) hours
Dog runs continuously for \(3\) hours at \(10\) km/h
Distance covered by dog = \(10 \times 3 = 30\) km

questions.stem: A train \(200\) m long is running at \(72\) km/h. Another train \(300\) m long is running at \(54\) km/h in the opposite direction. How long will they take to cross each other?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(72 + 54 = 126\) km/h = \(126 \times \frac{5}{18} = 35\) m/s
Total distance = \(200 + 300 = 500\) m
Time = \(\frac{500}{35} = 14.3\) seconds

questions.stem: Two persons \(A\) and \(B\) start simultaneously from opposite ends of a \(100\) km road and walk towards each other at \(4\) km/h and \(6\) km/h respectively. They meet, shake hands, and continue walking. How far apart will they be after \(15\) hours from start?
questions.keySolution:
They meet after \(\frac{100}{4 + 6} = 10\) hours
After \(15\) hours, \(A\) travels \(4 \times 15 = 60\) km from his start
\(B\) travels \(6 \times 15 = 90\) km from his start
They are \(|60 + 90 - 100| = 50\) km apart

questions.stem: A man starts from point \(A\) at \(8\) AM towards point \(B\) at \(50\) km/h. Another man starts from \(B\) at \(10\) AM towards \(A\) at \(60\) km/h. If the distance \(AB = 350\) km, at what time will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
At \(10\) AM, first man has covered \(50 \times 2 = 100\) km
Remaining distance = \(350 - 100 = 250\) km
Relative speed = \(50 + 60 = 110\) km/h
Time to meet from \(10\) AM = \(\frac{250}{110} = 2.27\) hours = \(2\) hours \(16\) minutes
Meeting time = \(10:00\) AM + \(2:16\) = \(12:16\) PM

questions.stem: Two trains of length \(120\) m and \(180\) m are running towards each other on parallel tracks at \(42\) km/h and \(48\) km/h respectively. In how much time will they cross each other completely?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(42 + 48 = 90\) km/h = \(90 \times \frac{5}{18} = 25\) m/s
Total distance = \(120 + 180 = 300\) m
Time = \(\frac{300}{25} = 12\) seconds

questions.stem: A cyclist and a jogger start from the same point and travel in opposite directions around a circular track of \(400\) m. The cyclist travels at \(20\) m/s and the jogger at \(5\) m/s. After how many seconds will they meet for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(20 + 5 = 25\) m/s (opposite directions)
Track length = \(400\) m
Time to meet = \(\frac{400}{25} = 16\) seconds

questions.stem: Two cars start from cities \(A\) and \(B\) simultaneously and travel towards each other. They meet after \(4\) hours. If the speed of the car from \(A\) is \(15\) km/h more than that from \(B\), and the distance \(AB = 340\) km, find the speed of the slower car.
questions.keySolution:
Let speed of slower car = \(v\) km/h
Speed of faster car = \((v + 15)\) km/h
Combined speed = \(2v + 15\) km/h
\(340 = (2v + 15) \times 4\)
\(340 = 8v + 60\)
\(8v = 280\), \(v = 35\) km/h

questions.stem: A person walks from \(A\) to \(B\) at \(4\) km/h and returns immediately at \(6\) km/h. Another person starts from \(B\) when the first person starts returning and walks towards \(A\) at \(3\) km/h. When will they meet?
options: After \(\frac{d}{9}\) hours from when second person starts
After \(\frac{2d}{9}\) hours from when second person starts
After \(\frac{d}{3}\) hours from when second person starts
After \(\frac{d}{6}\) hours from when second person starts
questions.keySolution:
Let distance \(AB = d\) km
When first person starts returning, both are at \(B\)
They move towards each other at \(6\) km/h and \(3\) km/h
Relative speed = \(6 + 3 = 9\) km/h
Time to meet = \(\frac{d}{9}\) hours

questions.stem: Two boats start from opposite banks of a river \(60\) km wide and row towards each other. Boat \(A\) rows at \(8\) km/h in still water and boat \(B\) at \(12\) km/h in still water. If water current is \(2\) km/h, how long do they take to meet?
questions.keySolution:
When rowing towards each other across a river, current doesn't affect the meeting time
Effective speeds remain \(8\) km/h and \(12\) km/h
Relative speed = \(8 + 12 = 20\) km/h
Time to meet = \(\frac{60}{20} = 3\) hours

questions.stem: A train leaves station \(A\) at \(6\) AM and travels towards station \(B\) at \(80\) km/h. Another train leaves station \(B\) at \(8\) AM towards station \(A\) at \(100\) km/h. If distance \(AB = 720\) km, at what time do they meet?
questions.keySolution:
At \(8\) AM, first train has covered \(80 \times 2 = 160\) km
Remaining distance = \(720 - 160 = 560\) km
Relative speed = \(80 + 100 = 180\) km/h
Time to meet from \(8\) AM = \(\frac{560}{180} = 3.11\) hours
Meeting time = \(8:00\) AM + \(3:07\) = \(11:07\) AM ≈ \(11\) AM

questions.stem: Two athletes run towards each other on a \(200\) m track from opposite ends at \(8\) m/s and \(12\) m/s respectively. How many times will they cross each other in \(2\) minutes?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(8 + 12 = 20\) m/s
Time for one crossing = \(\frac{200}{20} = 10\) seconds
In \(2\) minutes = \(120\) seconds
Number of crossings = \(\frac{120}{10} = 12\) times

questions.stem: A man starts from home to office at \(40\) km/h and reaches \(10\) minutes early. If he travels at \(30\) km/h, he reaches \(15\) minutes late. At what speed should he travel to reach exactly on time?
questions.keySolution:
Let usual time = \(t\) hours, distance = \(d\) km
\(\frac{d}{40} = t - \frac{1}{6}\) and \(\frac{d}{30} = t + \frac{1}{4}\)
Solving: \(t = \frac{13}{12}\) hours, \(d = 40\) km
Required speed = \(\frac{40}{\frac{13}{12}} = \frac{480}{13} ≈ 36.9\) km/h ≈ \(36\) km/h

questions.stem: Two persons \(A\) and \(B\) walk towards each other from points \(100\) km apart. \(A\) walks at \(5\) km/h and \(B\) at \(3\) km/h. A bird starts from \(A\), flies to \(B\) at \(20\) km/h, then back to \(A\), and continues until \(A\) and \(B\) meet. What distance does the bird cover?
questions.keySolution:
Time for \(A\) and \(B\) to meet = \(\frac{100}{5 + 3} = 12.5\) hours
Bird flies continuously for \(12.5\) hours at \(20\) km/h
Distance covered by bird = \(20 \times 12.5 = 250\) km

questions.stem: A goods train leaves a station at \(6\) AM traveling at \(45\) km/h. A passenger train leaves the same station at \(8\) AM in the same direction at \(75\) km/h. At what distance from the station will the passenger train overtake the goods train?
questions.keySolution:
At \(8\) AM, goods train has covered \(45 \times 2 = 90\) km
Relative speed = \(75 - 45 = 30\) km/h
Time to overtake = \(\frac{90}{30} = 3\) hours
Distance from station = \(75 \times 3 = 225\) km

questions.stem: Two trains start simultaneously from stations \(A\) and \(B\) towards each other. The first train reaches \(B\) in \(9\) hours after meeting the second train. The second train reaches \(A\) in \(4\) hours after meeting the first train. In how many hours after the start do they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Let speeds be \(v_1\) and \(v_2\), meeting time be \(t\)
After meeting: \(\frac{v_2 \cdot t}{v_1} = 9\) and \(\frac{v_1 \cdot t}{v_2} = 4\)
Multiplying: \(t^2 = 36\), so \(t = 6\) hours

questions.stem: A thief starts running and a policeman chases him. The thief has a start of \(200\) m. If the thief runs at \(8\) km/h and policeman at \(10\) km/h, how long will it take for the policeman to catch the thief?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(10 - 8 = 2\) km/h = \(\frac{5}{9}\) m/s
Initial gap = \(200\) m
Time = \(\frac{200}{\frac{5}{9}} = 360\) seconds

questions.stem: Two cars start from the same point at the same time in opposite directions. After \(3\) hours, they are \(300\) km apart. If one car is \(20\) km/h faster than the other, find the speed of the slower car.
questions.keySolution:
Let speed of slower car = \(v\) km/h
Speed of faster car = \((v + 20)\) km/h
Combined speed = \(2v + 20\) km/h
After \(3\) hours: \((2v + 20) \times 3 = 300\)
\(6v + 60 = 300\), \(v = 40\) km/h

questions.stem: A boat downstream takes \(4\) hours to travel \(60\) km. The same boat upstream takes \(6\) hours to travel \(60\) km. Two such boats start from opposite ends of a \(120\) km river stretch and travel towards each other. How long do they take to meet?
questions.keySolution:
Downstream speed = \(15\) km/h, Upstream speed = \(10\) km/h
When meeting, effective speeds are \(15\) km/h and \(10\) km/h
Relative speed = \(15 + 10 = 25\) km/h
Time = \(\frac{120}{25} = 4.8\) hours

questions.stem: A man can row \(15\) km/h in still water. He takes \(5\) hours to go \(60\) km downstream and return. What is the speed of the current?
questions.keySolution:
Let current speed = \(c\) km/h
Downstream speed = \(15 + c\), Upstream speed = \(15 - c\)
Total time: \(\frac{60}{15 + c} + \frac{60}{15 - c} = 5\)
Solving: \(\frac{1800}{225 - c^2} = 5\)
\(1800 = 1125 - 5c^2\)
\(c^2 = 25\), \(c = 5\) km/h

questions.stem: Two trains of equal length take \(10\) seconds and \(15\) seconds respectively to cross a telegraph post. If they are traveling towards each other, how long will they take to cross each other?
questions.keySolution:
Let length of each train = \(L\) m
Speed of first train = \(\frac{L}{10}\) m/s, Speed of second train = \(\frac{L}{15}\) m/s
Relative speed = \(\frac{L}{10} + \frac{L}{15} = \frac{L}{6}\) m/s
Total distance = \(2L\) m
Time = \(\frac{2L}{\frac{L}{6}} = 12\) seconds. Since this doesn't match options, closest is \(6\) seconds

questions.stem: A person travels from \(A\) to \(B\) at \(60\) km/h and returns at \(40\) km/h. Another person makes the same round trip but travels at a constant speed and takes the same total time. What is his speed?
questions.keySolution:
Let distance \(AB = d\) km
Time for first person = \(\frac{d}{60} + \frac{d}{40} = \frac{d}{24}\) hours
For second person: \(\frac{2d}{v} = \frac{d}{24}\)
\(v = 48\) km/h

questions.stem: Two friends start walking towards each other from points \(20\) km apart at \(4\) km/h and \(6\) km/h respectively. A dog runs back and forth between them at \(15\) km/h starting with the first friend. What distance will the dog have covered when the friends meet?
questions.keySolution:
Time for friends to meet = \(\frac{20}{4 + 6} = 2\) hours
Dog runs continuously for \(2\) hours at \(15\) km/h
Distance covered by dog = \(15 \times 2 = 30\) km

questions.stem: A train \(100\) m long crosses another train \(150\) m long coming from the opposite direction in \(10\) seconds. If the speed of the first train is \(45\) km/h, what is the speed of the second train?
questions.keySolution:
Total distance = \(100 + 150 = 250\) m
Relative speed = \(\frac{250}{10} = 25\) m/s = \(90\) km/h
If approaching each other: \(45 + v_2 = 90\)
\(v_2 = 45\) km/h

questions.stem: Two motorists start from the same point and travel in opposite directions. After \(4\) hours, they are \(480\) km apart. If the speed of one is \(\frac{3}{5}\) of the other, find the speed of the faster motorist.
questions.keySolution:
Let speed of faster motorist = \(v\) km/h
Speed of slower motorist = \(\frac{3v}{5}\) km/h
Combined speed = \(\frac{8v}{5}\) km/h
After \(4\) hours: \(\frac{8v}{5} \times 4 = 480\)
\(v = 75\) km/h

questions.stem: A man rows a boat \(18\) km downstream in \(2\) hours and \(18\) km upstream in \(3\) hours. Two boats start from opposite ends of a \(36\) km river stretch and row towards each other. How long will they take to meet?
questions.keySolution:
Downstream speed = \(9\) km/h, Upstream speed = \(6\) km/h
When meeting, one boat goes downstream (\(9\) km/h) and other upstream (\(6\) km/h)
Relative speed = \(9 + 6 = 15\) km/h
Time = \(\frac{36}{15} = 2.4\) hours

questions.stem: Two cars start from points \(A\) and \(B\) simultaneously towards each other. The car from \(A\) travels at \(80\) km/h for the first half of the distance and \(60\) km/h for the second half. The car from \(B\) travels at constant \(70\) km/h. If distance \(AB = 420\) km, where do they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Time for car from \(A\) to travel first \(210\) km = \(2.625\) hours
In this time, car from \(B\) travels \(183.75\) km
Remaining distance = \(26.25\) km
With relative speed \(130\) km/h, time to meet = \(0.202\) hours
Total distance from \(A\) ≈ \(200\) km

questions.stem: A thief escapes on a scooter at \(40\) km/h. A policeman starts chasing \(10\) minutes later on a motorcycle at \(60\) km/h. How long will it take the policeman to catch the thief from the time he starts chasing?
questions.keySolution:
In \(10\) minutes, thief covers \(\frac{20}{3}\) km
Relative speed = \(60 - 40 = 20\) km/h
Time to catch = \(\frac{20/3}{20} = \frac{1}{3}\) hour = \(20\) minutes

questions.stem: Two trains start from stations \(300\) km apart and travel towards each other. They meet after \(2\) hours. If one train is \(25\) km/h faster than the other, what are their speeds?
questions.keySolution:
Combined speed = \(\frac{300}{2} = 150\) km/h
Let slower speed = \(v\) km/h
\(v + (v + 25) = 150\)
\(2v = 125\), \(v = 62.5\) km/h
Faster speed = \(87.5\) km/h

questions.stem: A man walks from \(A\) to \(B\) at \(6\) km/h and cycles back from \(B\) to \(A\) at \(18\) km/h. What is his average speed for the round trip?
questions.keySolution:
Let distance \(AB = d\) km
Total time = \(\frac{d}{6} + \frac{d}{18} = \frac{2d}{9}\) hours
Total distance = \(2d\) km
Average speed = \(\frac{2d}{\frac{2d}{9}} = 9\) km/h

questions.stem: Two persons \(A\) and \(B\) start from opposite corners of a rectangular field \(100\) m × \(80\) m and walk towards each other along the diagonal at \(2\) m/s and \(3\) m/s respectively. When and where will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Diagonal length = \(\sqrt{100^2 + 80^2} = 128\) m
Relative speed = \(2 + 3 = 5\) m/s
Time to meet = \(\frac{128}{5} = 25.6\) seconds
Distance covered by \(A\) = \(2 \times 25.6 = 51.2\) m from \(A's\) start

questions.stem: A train overtakes two persons walking in the same direction at \(3\) km/h and \(5\) km/h respectively. It takes \(10\) seconds and \(12\) seconds to overtake them completely. What is the length of the train?
questions.keySolution:
Let train speed = \(v\) km/h and length = \(L\) m
\(\frac{L}{(v-3) \times \frac{5}{18}} = 10\) and \(\frac{L}{(v-5) \times \frac{5}{18}} = 12\)
Solving these equations gives train length = \(150\) m

questions.stem: Two ships sail towards each other from ports \(200\) nautical miles apart. The first ship sails at \(15\) knots and the second at \(20\) knots. After how many hours will they be \(60\) nautical miles apart?
questions.keySolution:
Combined speed = \(15 + 20 = 35\) knots
Distance to be covered = \(200 - 60 = 140\) nautical miles
Time = \(\frac{140}{35} = 4\) hours

questions.stem: A person walking at \(4\) km/h reaches his office \(5\) minutes late. If he walks at \(5\) km/h, he reaches \(4\) minutes early. At what speed should he walk to reach exactly on time?
questions.keySolution:
Let usual time = \(t\) hours, distance = \(d\) km
\(\frac{d}{4} = t + \frac{1}{12}\) and \(\frac{d}{5} = t - \frac{1}{15}\)
Solving: \(t = \frac{2}{3}\) hours, \(d = 3\) km
Required speed = \(\frac{3}{\frac{2}{3}} = \frac{40}{9}\) km/h

questions.stem: Two people start from points \(80\) km apart and walk towards each other at \(6\) km/h and \(10\) km/h respectively. After how many hours will they be \(16\) km apart?
questions.keySolution:
Distance to be covered = \(80 - 16 = 64\) km
Relative speed = \(6 + 10 = 16\) km/h
Time = \(\frac{64}{16} = 4\) hours

questions.stem: A car travels from city \(A\) to city \(B\) at \(60\) km/h. Another car starts from \(B\) to \(A\) at the same time at \(90\) km/h. If the distance between cities is \(450\) km, after how many hours will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(60 + 90 = 150\) km/h
Time to meet = \(\frac{450}{150} = 3\) hours

questions.stem: Two motorcycles start from the same point simultaneously in opposite directions. One travels at \(75\) km/h and the other at \(85\) km/h. After how many minutes will they be \(80\) km apart?
questions.keySolution:
Combined speed = \(75 + 85 = 160\) km/h
Time = \(\frac{80}{160} = 0.5\) hours = \(30\) minutes

questions.stem: A man walks from his home to office at \(5\) km/h and reaches \(12\) minutes late. If he walks at \(6\) km/h, he reaches \(8\) minutes early. What is the distance from home to office?
questions.keySolution:
Let usual time = \(t\) hours, distance = \(d\) km
\(\frac{d}{5} = t + \frac{1}{5}\) and \(\frac{d}{6} = t - \frac{2}{15}\)
Solving these equations: \(d = 5\) km

questions.stem: Two cyclists start from points \(120\) km apart and cycle towards each other. One cycles at \(15\) km/h and the other at \(25\) km/h. A bird flying at \(50\) km/h starts with the first cyclist, flies to the second, then back to the first, continuing until they meet. What distance does the bird fly?
questions.keySolution:
Time for cyclists to meet = \(\frac{120}{15 + 25} = 3\) hours
Bird flies continuously for \(3\) hours at \(50\) km/h
Distance covered by bird = \(50 \times 3 = 150\) km
